summary.intent: Evaluate how well the Wisp plugins (muse, scribe, smith, etc.) served front-end work and design ideation across the orin-dx and techworx sites, and identify gaps, especially their rigidity for early/experimental work. The session later moved to finishing the v5 plugin rewrite (docs, mason, repo migrations) and then refining wisp.
summary.outcome: Four investigations found the old plugin set was spec-first and converge-only, with no visual or sketch mode, and that ideation ran outside the plugins. The v5 work was documented, committed and pushed (#419 plus four repo migrations), but #416 and #419 were not yet merged, so the 5.0.0 release was blocked, and the three small wisp tweaks were committed on a branch.

repo: Old plugin set was a spec-driven lifecycle (weaver, vanguard, scribe/muse, navigator, smith, courier) with typed JSON handoffs in shared/schemas and default-fail gates; no plugin had a browser, screenshot, visual or generative mode.
spec@1 has no fields for tokens, layout, breakpoints, visual references or motion, so a spec could pass muse's exit-gate while saying nothing about appearance.
muse docs referenced a ranger accessibility taxonomy that never existed, so implemented a11y was never checked.
Project session dirs mostly hold subagent transcripts: orin-dx has 2 real sessions and pages about 7, despite ~810 jsonl files.

Gates checked spec internal consistency (e.g. SPEC-001 needed 13 verdicts) but did not render anything, so visual defects such as non-full-screen NavSheet and NaN% glass opacity were caught by the user's eye or later audits.
Gate wins were behavioural: contrast recomputation (2.82:1), cross-spec contradictions, stale breakpoints, and plan ordering defects.
Entire opens PRs as trails; repos like Pages have a rule against opening PRs with gh.
A wisp manifest test pinned version 1.0.0 and failed on any version bump; the trim branch already removes that pin.
v5 constitution and agent-best-practices now say agents exist for a context or risk reason, and schemas are only for handoffs read by code or a hook.
Hook facts: validate-handback.py denies an invalid handback up to 3 times per agent (MAX_DENIALS=3), RETRY_CAP=1, wisp:verifier is the only routed agent, and WISP_HANDBACK_TRACE is the trace switch.

code.finding: Docstring and a comment wrongly said muse has an exit gate/registers the handback hook; fixed because in v5 muse has no hooks.json and ROUTES lists only wisp:verifier.
Hardcoded wisp version string 1.0.0 broke just check on version bump; the hardcoded pin was removed.
Still has a spec_hash field with no producer after the staleness rule was removed; removal is a breaking schema change and was left.

workflow: Run mechanical transcript scans for skill/agent usage first, then delegate parallel subagents for plugin inventory, per-project sessions and outcome audits.
Subagent hand-back reports are unverified model output; verify facts (e.g. the denial cap) against files before repeating them.
Teammate agents may report done while still editing; check git status for uncommitted changes after a commit and re-run just check.
Agents asked to run just ci can go quiet; nudge them to check the result and commit.
Check the live state of origin/main and trail status before claiming something is merged; here #416 and #419 were not merged despite the user's 'all merged'.
Prose spec approval fails for visual work; rendered option boards with short-code replies worked well for design ideation.
Stacked PRs (#419 on #416) must be merged in order before a release or the tag misses content.

friction: Initial corpus assumption was wrong: ~810 sessions were mostly subagent transcripts.
Large 60-130 KB spec and plan files stalled agent streams; 17 failed agent tasks and 32 stall mentions.
Gate loops churned on wording and citation residue; SPEC-005 reached retry 6, and the orchestrator carried on past the escalate signal without asking the user.
Specs were written before visuals settled, then rewritten after the user's visual review; ceremony cost ~75 minutes and ~110 agent calls before any visual existed.
Design decisions were lost across sessions, frustrating the user.
The user said 'All merged' but #416 and #419 were not merged.
The first Edit on the wisp skill failed because the string had been typed incorrectly (specs-and-plans.md twice).
The first just check on the wisp tweaks failed on the pinned 1.0.0 version test.
Branch creation needed several attempts, because the first attempt left an existing branch.
v5-docs and v5-readme edited the root README concurrently.
The repo-wide pre-commit gate cost many waits during parallel smith runs.
open_items: Merge #416 then #419, then run just release --dry-run and just release for 5.0.0.
Wisp tweaks commit made on a branch; check result and push/open a trail.
Decide whether to delete or keep the unwired hooks shared/hooks/subagent-start.sh and pre-command.sh.
Decide whether to remove mason's worker agents scaffolder and schema-designer.
About 35 orphaned schemas for the deleted pipeline and several unused references remain; spec_hash in plan@1 undecided.
Pages PR #45 was opened with gh against that repo's rule: close and redo as a trail, or keep.
Delete merged remote branches including the stray v5-core, and resolve Entire findings on trail #386.
Stale trails #388, #389 and #390 appear to be old guide-era work; user to decide whether to close.
Callisto's just ci ran before its commit and was not re-run on the committed tree.
Live use of v5 in the four repos is not verified; measuring rounds, turns and tokens needs a week or two of use.
Codex and Antigravity install lines, the .claude/settings.json snippet and the quick-start examples in the README are unverified.
Design gaps identified: sketch/explore mode, visual-intent criteria in specs, render-based gating, a promote-prototype-to-spec path, and cross-session decision memory.
